title: Gold And Silver Egg
description: Prepared with pike, ham, and eggs.
steps: Break the eggs carefully. Put the whites in one bowl and the yolks in another bowl. To each bowl add an equal amount of cold, boiled water and mix well.

Chop the Chinese ham into pieces as small as possible. Mix with the yolks of the eggs. Salt to suit the taste.

Now put the Chinese ham on one side of the dish and the pike on the other side. Do not let them mix. Steam for 20 minutes. When done there will be gold color on one side of the dish and silver on the other side.

title: Gold And Silver Frankfurters
description: Prepared with pork, liver, and wine.

ingredients.name: small intestine lining of a pig

steps: Get the outside lining of the small intestine of a pig. Wash thoroughly with salt and then put into hot water for 10 minutes. Tie one end, force air through from the other end, and tie. Dry in the hot sun.

Cut pork into pieces 3/8 inch by 3/8 inch by 3/8 inch. To every pound of pork add an equal amount of pig liver, which has been rubbed with salt, washed thoroughly, and cut into pieces the same size as the pork. To this add 3 ounces of salt, 1 tablespoonful of Fun Wine, and a few threads of orange skin. Mix well.
By means of a funnel fill this into the lining. Put a knob about every six inches. Punch plenty of small holes with a needle, to let in the air.
Expose in the hot sun for 1 day. Put in a windy place for 4 days.
Keep them in a china jar for at least 5 days before serving.
Steam in a double-boiler for 3/4 hour. Serve with fried potatoes or fried gray potatoes underneath.

After the continued trot of two leagues, arrive at the place where deep dishes await to receive it. Remove the stoppers and two cascades of frozen foam fill the containers.
Season with sugar and cinnamon and serve to the table.
Alternatively, in the early morning hours, place a quantity of good milk on ice seasoned with saltpeter in a deep tin or zinc dish.
You may add one cup of cream and season it with sugar and cinnamon.
Make two bundles of straw used for brooms to use as spatulas.
Beat the milk from both sides of the dish with these two spatulas.
In ten minutes, the milk will have turned to foam and this foam will have reached complete freezing.

title: Pastel de Choclo a la Sucrense (Corn Cake Sucre Style)
description: A cake made with corn, cornmeal or cornstarch, and egg yolks.

Return the pulp to the mortar and grind again, also adding one cup of milk, and strain.
Into this corn juice, add white cornmeal or cornstarch spoon by spoon, stirring as you add the flour and beating until it has thickened.
Season with salt and a little sugar, at most one or two spoonfuls, to bring out the natural sweetness of the corn.
Melt a large piece of butter and mix it into the mixture, stirring and beating until the butter is incorporated.
If the mixture has thickened too much, add a little milk and, always stirring, place it to cook over moderate heat.
Taste frequently to know by flavor when it is cooked and ready.
Remove from heat, add butter, stir and let cool. Once cold, mix in four egg yolks and stir to incorporate them into the mixture.

Butter the bottom of a heat-resistant earthenware dish and spread a layer of the corn mixture. Over this arrange a filling of your choice, either squab prepared in sauce and stewed, or a chopped mixture seasoned with spices, Malaga raisins, almonds and olives.
On the filling, arrange symmetrically slices of hard-boiled eggs and olives. Cover the filling with another layer of corn mixture and put in the oven.

title: Pastel de Pichones (Squab Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with suet, egg yolks, and squabs.
steps: Take one pound of flour and knead it by adding little by little cold water lightly saturated with salt and sugar.
Make a stiff dough, which will be softened by kneading it with both hands on a table. Once softened a bit, mix in it a small quantity of suet and the yolks of two eggs.
Knead again with the suet and egg, then extend with a rolling pin until it is thin.

Then spread over that entire flattened surface, by means of a feather or with the hand, melted suet; sprinkle flour over that suet, fold in two and pass the rolling pin again, extending and thinning the dough, and again spread suet and sprinkle flour, up to six times.
Then turn the dish or vessel in which it is to be arranged over the dough; take the measure and cut around the dough with the tip of a knife.

Filling the dish, arrange the squab filling which will be prepared as follows: Wash the squabs and their offal, give them a boil, and after letting them cool, cut them apart; setting aside the offal, put the pieces and give them another boil in a sauce of butter, chopped white onion, pepper, a little cumin, Malaga raisins, half a tablespoon of vinegar, sufficient salt and the offal, which will be arranged between piece and piece, as well as olives and hard-boiled eggs in slices.

title: Pastelitos de Ayuno (Fasting Little Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with almonds, almond milk, and olive oil.
steps: Peel 6 dozen almonds in boiling water and after washing them, grind them in a mortar.

Grind the pulp still further, and strain and squeeze again.

Mix the almond milk that results from this operation with flour, kneading it, adding little by little as you knead, 3 or 4 tablespoons of pure, fresh olive oil; and when the kneaded dough, with the help of the oil, is soft and flexible, stretch it with a rolling pin, fold it six times, making it into a puff pastry, which thinned with the rolling pin, is cut into small squares, and filled with the following preparation:
Take chard leaves, wash them and give them a boil in salted water, taking care to cover the vessel to prevent the chard from turning black on contact with air.
Once cooked, remove from heat; remove from the leaves stems and fibers, and well cleaned of all this, chop finely.
Cook potatoes unpeeled; and once cooked peel them and chop very well, and mix with the chard, adding very well-cooked green peas. Season with pepper, salt, oil and vinegar.
With everything well incorporated, fill the little pastries, which are put in a very hot oven, because their cooking should be brief: just the time for the pastries to brown: ten minutes.

title: Relleno a la Manolita (Manolita-Style Stuffed Lamb Legs)
description: Prepared with lamb, meat, and pork fat.

ingredients.name: Ground meat mixture with raisins, crushed almonds, ground roasted peanuts, salt, and pepper
Two tablespoons of finely chopped fine herbs
Lean ham, chopped into small pieces
Two chicken legs, chopped into small pieces
Six hard-boiled egg yolks, well ground

steps: Clean the lamb legs and carefully remove the upper bone with a pointed knife without tearing the meat.
Fill the hollow with a picadillo seasoned with raisins, crushed almonds, roasted and ground peanuts, salt, and pepper.
Stuff the legs and sew them well closed to prevent the filling from escaping.
In a pan, melt a piece of pork fat and a piece of butter.
Cook ground veal and two tablespoons of finely chopped fine herbs in this mixture.
After two boils, add one tablespoon of flour, one cup of hot water, and a lemon cut into thin slices.
Stir well and after two more boils, pour this preparation over the legs arranged at the bottom of a pan.
Let them cook for four hours.
Remove from heat and drain the legs, remove the stitching thread, place them in a serving dish.
To prepare the sauce: bring to a slow boil in a pan 250 grams of butter, 25 grams of lean ham, 500 grams of veal, and two chicken legs, all chopped into fine pieces.
Season with salt, pepper, spices, a bay leaf, two carrots, and two onions.
When the meats have taken on color in the butter, add half a dozen well-ground hard-boiled egg yolks, stirring vigorously to blend the mixture.
Gradually pour in one liter of milk, stirring constantly, and let it cook at a slow fire for one hour, stirring always.
Pass through a fine sieve and pour hot over the stuffed legs at the moment of serving.

title: Repollo a la Romana (Cabbage Roman Style)
description: Prepared with cabbage, sausage, and bread.
steps: Choose a well-formed cabbage and, passing a string around it to prevent it from opening, blanch it in salted water.

When it has received this first, light cooking so that the leaves do not lose their firmness, remove it from the water, receive it in a cloth, with which gently press it to dry it; place it standing on a plate; remove the string that closes it, and open it slightly in the shape of a rose.
Prepare a filling as follows: grind in a mortar sausage meat, cooked poultry offal, and bread crumb, seasoned with pepper, a pinch of cumin and salt if that of the sausage is not sufficient.
Add two half-beaten egg yolks to incorporate and bind the filling. Add half a spoonful of oil, half a spoonful of vinegar and a piece of butter the size of a hazelnut. Mix very well.

With this filling, coat the interior and exterior of each cabbage leaf. Then, with light and careful hand, fold the leaves back over the heart, also filled with minced chicken livers. The cabbage thus recovers its form.

Tie a string around it again to preserve it; and in a tall pot so as not to crush the cabbage in its cooking, putting on the bottom a layer of bacon slices sprinkled with cooked sauce, place the cabbage always standing; cover it with the lid, with hot coals on top, and moderate heat below, cook slowly.

Serve with a sauce made as follows: Put in a pot four spoonfuls of good broth with a little chopped parsley; a shallot; cooked mushrooms and truffles cut into thin slices, and a spoonful of butter, seasoning with salt and pepper. Stir, letting it boil for half an hour during which the broth will have reduced. Then add a spoonful of oil. Stir for a moment, and add half a glass of Champagne wine. Stir for half a minute; remove the pot from the fire and arrange in the serving dish, in which the cabbage is immediately served standing, wedged with pickled gherkins.

description: Prepared with veal, olive oil, and vinegar.

steps: Cut a piece of veal loin 4 centimeters thick and as long as needed according to the number of sandwiches required.
